incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: P1 - dedpool node gpu-node-17 (aurora-dedicated-7) reported repeated GPU disconnects and ECC spikes. Affected tenant: greenbridge. Pager: @Alex, @Maya.

Alex: Acked. I'm grabbing the bridge. Initial impact: greenbridge has ~12% of their inference tail requests failing, increased latency 200-400ms for surviving requests. No full outage yet, but errors spiking.

Maya: I'm oncall and taking lead. Creating bridge and paging hw team. Putting immediate mitigation plan: 1) isolate node, 2) drain running jobs, 3) migrate affected tenant shards to warm spare, 4) open HW RMA if hardware fault.

Maya: Running quick status check
```
$ redwoodctl node status gpu-node-17 --pool aurora-dedicated-7 --json
{
  "node": "gpu-node-17",
  "state": "degrading",
  "gpu_errors": 231,
  "last_disconnect": "2026-11-02T10:02:12Z",
  "thermal_reading_c": 95,
  "kv_cache_inflight": 18
}
```

Sam: seeing driver disconnect + ECC in syslogs on the node. Snippet:
```
[Nov 02 10:01:58] NVC: GPU: ecc corrected errors rising: gpu0: 120 -> 231 in 5m
[Nov 02 10:02:12] nvidia: GPU 0: reset required, driver lost device
```

Sam: Could be thermal or NVLink fabric flapping. If we keep the node in the pool some jobs will keep getting retried and inflate tail latency. Recommend immediate drain and tenant migration.

Maya: Initiating drain now (grace 60s). Will also trigger automatic fallback routing for greenbridge to their reserved warm spare pool.

Maya: Command: `redwoodctl drain-node --node gpu-node-17 --pool aurora-dedicated-7 --grace-period 60s --reason "gpu disconnects / ECC spike"`

infra-bot: drain started, tracker https://infra.redwood/prod/drains/DRN-8742 - 6 tasks currently running on node, eviction policy: priority=tenant-critical then best-effort.

Alex: Lia, can you start customer comms? Lia: queued a short notify to Greenbridge CSE and AM, templated message below.

Lia: Draft to Greenbridge CSE:
"We've detected elevated GPU errors on a node serving your dedicated pool (aurora-dedicated-7). We're draining the affected node and migrating your workloads to a warm spare to avoid request failures. No action required from you now; we'll update when migration completes. ETA ~5-10 min. - Redwood Oncall"

Lia: Sent to CSE + AM, CC'd account lead. Greenbridge replied in email thread asking for ETA and impact percent. I told them ~5-15m and that tail errors should stop once migration completes.

Maya: Migration triggered: `redwoodctl migrate-tenant --tenant greenbridge --from-node gpu-node-17 --to-pool aurora-warm-spare-1 --maint-mode true`

infra-bot: tenant migration job ID MIG-9921 started. Progress updates posted to bridge.

Sam: Observing steady evictions, KV cache warmup on target pool. Watch for model cold start errors — we may need to bump replica count temporarily.

Maya: Adding temporary throttle to embeddings path for greenbridge to reduce pressure while cache warms:
```
$ redwoodctl tenant-config set --tenant greenbridge --route embeddings --rate-limit 30r/s
```

Alex: PagerDuty note: incident severity P1, impacted customer greenbridge (enterprise/vpc). Root cause unknown, suspected HW thermal or NVLink. Opening HW ticket and cloud provider VM health check.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Alex and Maya. Oncall rotation: handing to Jin at 10:20.

Maya: Handoff: I'm staying for 5 more mins to confirm migration finished, then passing to Jin to coordinate postmortem and HW RMA.

Jin: Taking over at 10:20. I see MIG-9921 at 87% and drain complete on gpu-node-17. Verifying greenbridge error rate now.

Sam: Logs show last driver disconnect at +2m after drain started, then no further disconnects. Latency numbers: tail p95->p99 back to baseline in ~3 minutes after migration finished.

Jin: Verified with metrics: greenbridge error-rate dropped from 12% -> 0.6%. No active requests on gpu-node-17. Marking node quarantined.

infra-bot: Node gpu-node-17 marked quarantine, cordoned from scheduler. Ticket HW-5872 opened with provider: "possible thermal runaway / card failure - ECC spike and driver resets".

Maya: Next steps: 1) HW RMA, 2) keep node cordoned until RMA complete, 3) create follow-up for postmortem with owner Sam (eng-runtime), 4) update SLA impact window to the account.

Lia: Sent customer update: migration complete, tail errors mitigated, we're continuing monitoring and will follow up with detailed timeline. Greenbridge responded: thanks, please include any actions on their side if needed. I told them no action required.

Alex: Postmortem owner: Sam. Action items: investigate NVLink / thermal logs, confirm whether mitigation (drain) should be automated earlier in similar metric patterns, add alert for consecutive driver-resets > 3 in 5m to auto-isolate node.

Jin: I'll flush the evacuation playbook into the runbook and attach MIG-9921 logs. Assigning follow-ups in tracker: PMT-1145 (postmortem), HW-5872 (RMA), OPS-2210 (auto-isolate alert).

Maya: Closing active page. If we see any regression I'll reopen. Great coordination, team. :thumbsup: :rotating_light:

Alex: Noted. Closing incident thread; leaving bot reminders for postmortem in 48h.

incident-bot: Incident P1 closed by Alex. Summary: gpu-node-17 in aurora-dedicated-7 experienced ECC spikes and driver disconnects leading to tenant tail errors for Greenbridge. Drain + migration to warm-spare completed; error rates recovered. HW ticket HW-5872 opened. Postmortem owner: Sam.
summary: Dedicated pool gpu-node hardware/ECC spike -> drain, tenant migration to warm spare, HW RMA opened, postmortem assigned
